title: Date page: today by default, chart and events, cast on demand

history.detail:
PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 28, against HEAD c633ecb (diff db6112f..c633ecb). Sprint file re-read fresh at audit time, including the R12 amendment (72b1d3a). Working tree clean, all code committed.

VERDICT: PASS. No demonstrated defect.

Verified by running, not by reading the handoff: npm test 24 files / 248 tests green; lint clean; npm run build clean, route table shows / and /date/[date] and /date all as dynamic (server-rendered on demand), nothing prerendered except _not-found.

R1: /date/[date] via shared ReadingView. Extraction diffed mechanically against the old /reading/[id] JSX: the only changes are the jdNote and belowDateBand slots, reading.* renamed to props, and the disabled branch moved into DisabledReadingSection verbatim. Not a fork. Malformed and out-of-range dates go through parseDatePageParam (adapter's own round-trip check plus assertDateInSupportedRange at the 12:00 UT calculation instant) and reach notFound(). Non-DateInputError exceptions are rethrown, not swallowed.
R1/R9: /reading/[id] lookup and 404 path diffed against db6112f: identical apart from one comment. It still passes the sealed note and FlowIndicator. ReadingPanel offerNewChart defaults to true, so /reading/[id] renders as before.
R2: app/page.tsx calls connection() then redirect() (307). next.config.ts static redirect removed. No force-static, no build-time constant, no permanent redirect. The build output confirms / is dynamic.
R3: traced the GET render. loadDatePage does one RPC (get_reading_by_date) plus computePositions and fetchDayEvents. isHoroscopeEnabled reads env. castHoroscope is only bound as a form action. No insert, no set_reading_horoscope and no OpenAI client is reachable from the render.
R4: migration 20261115211107 is security definer, search_path pinned, takes a date, filters horoscope is not null, orders by horoscope_generated_at desc nulls last with deterministic tiebreakers, limit 1. No select policy. Grant to anon and authenticated. Ends with the schema_migrations insert. Found row: page renders the stored positions and events, and events are not re-fetched (load.test covers this).
R5: castHoroscopeForDate checks isHoroscopeEnabled before any DB call. Insert failures are classified via isDatabaseUnavailable insert. Always redirects to the date page. It also short-circuits when a horoscope already exists for the date (good, stops stale-tab regeneration).
R6: dateLookup operation added to the availability allowlist (excepts no codes, since the date is pre-validated). The unavailable branch renders computed chart and events plus a notice, with no cast form, and logs via logDatabaseUnavailable.
R7: plain GET form to /date. min and max are taken from the adapter constants, prefilled, required. /date validates and redirects, or 404s. Array or empty values give 404, never a 500.
R8: the date page passes no jdNote and does not import FlowIndicator. The word sealed appears only in a code comment.
R10: R4 cases present (newest of several, horoscope-less only, no rows, neighbouring date, anon direct select still empty). Unit tests cover the UTC boundary at 23:59:59.999 and 00:00, offsets, and the validator (malformed, out of range, both boundaries, non-strings). Guardrail files untouched.
R11: PRD committed once in 93a74cf, not modified since.
R12 migration 20261115212732: drops the anon insert policy, revokes INSERT from anon and authenticated, and revokes EXECUTE on set_reading_horoscope from anon, authenticated and PUBLIC. I read 20260816125144: its table GRANTs ran earlier and are superseded; its ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES lines only affect objects created later. Nothing re-grants. service_role keeps EXECUTE through the default privileges (set_reading_horoscope was created after them) and keeps its explicit table grant.
R12 clients: grep shows no anon insert into readings and no anon set_reading_horoscope RPC in app/ or lib/. The only hit outside lib/readings/insert.ts is the guardrail's own test fixture. createAdminClient is imported only by the health route and the three use-server action files. The lib/ writers take the client as a parameter. No use-client file reaches admin.
R12 inputs: saveReading and the cast take only the validated date from the form. /reading/[id] takes only the id, and its positions and events come from the stored row.
R12 tests: Sprint 4 insert test inverted with an explanatory comment, not deleted, and asserts 42501. New route-1 and route-2 denial tests on the anon client. Fixtures are seeded through the seed (service-role) client, and assertions run on anon only.
R12 attacks re-traced against the final code: route 1 is denied (no INSERT privilege and no policy). Route 2 is denied at its first step and independently at the RPC (no EXECUTE for anon or PUBLIC). Route 3 needs a planted row, and anon can no longer plant one. All three now fail at the database.

NOT VERIFIED BY ME: the RLS suite (supabase/tests). There is no Docker in this environment, so I could not start a local stack, and the commit is unpushed, so no CI run exists for it. I reviewed it statically only. Backstop: ci.yml's migrate job needs rls-tests, so a red suite blocks the production migration. LiveQA step 8 re-checks R12 against production. I have not seen Dev Team's handoff output, so I cannot confirm the R10 claim that the RLS suite is green.

Observations, not blocking:
(a) The date page reflects ?error= text from the URL into the error note, so a crafted link can show arbitrary (React-escaped, not stored) text on a real date page. This is the existing /reading/[id] pattern, which R5 told Dev Team to follow. It is a reflected, not stored, spoofing surface. Master Controller may want to decide whether the front-door page should map error codes to fixed messages instead. Not a requirement of this sprint.
(b) get_reading_by_date, like get_reading_by_id before it, also holds EXECUTE through PUBLIC and service_role by Postgres and project defaults. It is read-only, the same precedent as Sprint 4, and harmless.
(c) Every failed-cast retry inserts another orphan row with no horoscope. R5 explicitly accepts this.

No new Human Prerequisites. The service role key in Vercel Production is already listed in the sprint file.
